A_ties.how_ranks_are_made_deterministic: Ranks sort by score descending, then cve_id ascending (lexical), so they do not depend on row order or machine. The expected value (random order inside the tied group) is reported beside it and is the tie-neutral number.
A_ties.first_pass_order_note: first_pass_top500 and the table's 'reproduced' column use the first pass's own order: pandas sort_values with the default unstable quicksort on pool row order, descending. Its tie order is arbitrary and may depend on the numpy build and CPU.

C_early_stopping.note: max_iter=150 is the documented setting; n_iter_ is what each fit actually used under early_stopping='auto'.

D_seed_noise.seed_scheme: Run i uses text folds seed i (fold_only / both_vary) and HGB seeds 3i, 3i+1, 3i+2 (hgb_only / both_vary), each a mean of 3 HGB fits. Run 0 equals the primary run.

F_censoring.note: All windows end at the 2025-12-31 cap in the test pool, so later months have less time to reach KEV.

G_bootstrap._note: Percentile CI over 2000 row resamples, seed 0, the same resamples for every method. _cve_id ties by id, _expected and _mid are tie-neutral; they match unless a method has ties at the cutoff.

H_description_exploit_wording.pattern: exploited in the wild|actively exploited|known to be exploited|has been exploited|may have been exploited|is being exploited|CISA|KEV
H_description_exploit_wording.note: Cannot tell from the data whether the wording was there at publication or added later. Measurement only; nothing is removed.
